/itineraryStops/0/whyOnRoute.source_en: Two pickup points cover Seoul's two main visitor clusters — the Hongik University area in Mapo-gu and ⟦G0⟧ in Jung-gu — and Hongik first is the natural order for a northeast-bound run. The 06:00 start is not padding: Seoraksan is roughly three hours away and the value of going there in winter is being on the valley floor while the light is still on the snow. A later departure would put the park visit into the afternoon flatness and push the last stop past dark.

/itineraryStops/0/description.source_en:
Pickup is at one of two Seoul meeting points: **(1) Starbucks Hongik University Station Exit 8 (Mapo-gu)** at 06:00 — the Starbucks storefront sits immediately at the top of Exit 8; OR **(2) ⟦G0⟧ Station Exit 2 (Jung-gu)** at 06:30 — the NorthFace flagship store is the visible landmark next to the exit.

Both pickup points share the same heated coach and Hongik passengers board first. Please be at your chosen point **5 minutes before the scheduled time** — this is an early start on a cold morning and the day only works if the coach reaches Seoraksan by 09:30.

Dress for the whole day at boarding, not for the walk to the subway: you will be outdoors at −5 °C or colder at two of the three stops, and the last one is on ice. The guide distributes a printed Korean-English itinerary card and confirms the day's plan, including whether the Seoraksan cable car is running and what the village is charging at Eobi.

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/1.source_en: Tongildaebul: 14.6 m / 108 tons bronze — Korea's largest seated bronze Buddha (1997)
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/1.tm: Tongildaebul: 14,6 m / 108 Tonnen Bronze — Koreas größter sitzender Bronze-Buddha (1997)

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/2.source_en: Sinheungsa Temple (652 CE Silla) — one of Korea's oldest active Buddhist temples and a Jogye Order monastery
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/2.tm: Sinheungsa-Tempel (652 n. Chr., Silla) — einer der ältesten noch aktiven buddhistischen Tempel Koreas und ein Kloster des Jogye-Ordens

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/3.source_en: Optional Seorak Cable Car 1,132 m to Gwongeumseong Fortress platform (700 m, 1253 legend)
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/3.tm: Optional die Seorak-Seilbahn über 1.132 m zur Plattform der Festung Gwongeumseong (700 m, Legende von 1253)

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/4.source_en: 30 peaks, 2,000+ animal species, 1,400-1,562 plant species; rare wildlife (musk deer, goral, Asian black bear)
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/4.tm: 30 Gipfel, über 2.000 Tierarten, 1.400–1.562 Pflanzenarten; seltene Wildtiere (Moschushirsch, Goral, Kragenbär)

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/5.source_en: Park entrance FREE since May 2023 (was 3,500 KRW); cable car still paid
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/5.tm: Parkeintritt KOSTENLOS seit Mai 2023 (zuvor 3.500 KRW); die Seilbahn bleibt kostenpflichtig

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/6.source_en: **IUCN Category II (National Park) since 2005 + IUCN Green List of Protected Areas since 2014** — Korea's first national park to enter the Green List during the Pilot Phase, alongside Odaesan and Jirisan
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/6.tm: **IUCN-Kategorie II (Nationalpark) seit 2005 und IUCN Green List of Protected Areas seit 2014** — Koreas erster Nationalpark, der in der Pilotphase auf die Green List kam, zusammen mit Odaesan und Jirisan

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/7.source_en: **Korea's first UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since August 1982** + **listed as UNESCO World Heritage tentative site** — combined recognition unmatched by any other Korean national park
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/7.tm: **Koreas erstes UNESCO-Biosphärenreservat seit August 1982** und **auf der Tentativliste des UNESCO-Welterbes** — eine Kombination an Auszeichnungen, die kein anderer koreanischer Nationalpark erreicht

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/8.source_en: **Long-tailed goral conservation centerpiece**: stable population of ~260 individuals (vulnerable on IUCN Red List) — the park manages 10 Special Protection Zones covering 39 km² (10% of total park area) for endangered species
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/8.tm: **Zentrum des Schutzes für den Langschwanzgoral**: stabile Population von ~260 Tieren (auf der Roten Liste der IUCN als gefährdet geführt) — der Park unterhält 10 Sonderschutzzonen auf 39 km² (10 % der Gesamtfläche) für bedrohte Arten

/itineraryStops/1/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Do not plan around the cable car. Winter hours shift daily and it closes on wind and ice more often than in other seasons; queues can also run long on clear days. Treat it as a bonus, not a fixture. Dress for −5 °C to +5 °C at the base with a strong wind chill.

/itineraryStops/1/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Visitor centre, cafes, restaurants and gift shops at the Sogongwon entrance. Indoor warm-up space is limited on busy winter days.

/itineraryStops/1/whyOnRoute.source_en: Seoraksan opens the day because it is both the furthest stop and the most light-dependent one. At 09:30 the snow on the granite ridges is still clean and the valley has not yet clouded over, which is the whole reason to drive three hours for it. Two hours at the Sogongwon entrance is enough for the Tongildaebul bronze Buddha, Sinheungsa Temple and the lower valley paths at a winter pace — not enough for a summit attempt, which is deliberate. Going first also gets the day's longest drive done before anyone is tired or cold.

/itineraryStops/1/convenience/restroom.source_en: At main entrance area, cable car station, Sinheungsa Temple grounds, along major trails
/itineraryStops/1/convenience/restroom.tm: Im Bereich des Haupteingangs, an der Seilbahnstation, auf dem Gelände des Sinheungsa-Tempels und entlang der Hauptwege
